title: Agrobacterium tumefaciens-Mediated Genetic Engineering of Green Microalgae, Chlorella vulgaris
protocol: Autoclave all media and solutions prior to use unless stated otherwise.
Use sterile or autoclaved centrifuge tubes, pipette tips, etc., before use.
Inoculate Agrobacterium (AGL-1) into a 25 mL sterile shaker flask of LB media supplemented with rifampicin.
Grow the culture overnight at 28-30 °C and 150 rpm.
Dilute the overnight culture 100,000-fold by adding 0.5 µL to 50 mL autoclaved ultra-pure water.
Spread 10 µL of this diluted culture on an LB plate and incubate at 28-30 °C for 1-3 days.
Pick a colony and start a 20 mL overnight culture in LB with rifampicin at 28-30 °C.
Inoculate 500 mL LB media (no antibiotic) in a shaker flask with 9 mL of the overnight culture and grow until OD600 reaches 0.5.
Divide the culture evenly into ten 50 mL centrifuge tubes and chill on ice for 30 min.
Pre-cool the centrifuge to 4 °C.
Centrifuge the tubes at 4 °C and 4000 x g for 15 min.
Remove as much supernatant as possible using a pipette.
Resuspend each pellet in 50 mL of ice-cold water.
Centrifuge the cells at 4 °C and 4000 x g for 15 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 25 mL of ice-cold water in each tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 4 °C and 4000 x g for 15 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold 10% (w/v) glycerol in each tube.
Combine all tubes into one 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 4 °C and 4000 x g for 15 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 400 μL ice-cold 10% (w/v) glycerol.
Distribute the cells as 50 µL aliquots in sterile prechilled microtubes.
Freeze in liquid nitrogen.
Store in a -80 °C freezer.
Add 50 µL of AGL-1 A. tumefaciens electrocompetent cells into a prechilled 0.1 mm cuvette.
Add 2 µL of pCAMBIA1302 or similar plasmid (conc 15 ng/µL).
Electroporate at 2400 V using an electroporator (200 Ω, capacitance extender 250 µFD, capacitance 25 µFD, exponential decay).
Immediately add 1 mL of LB media to the cuvette.
Gently pipette up and down to mix.
Transfer the 1 mL of resuspended cells into a 1.5 mL microtube.
Incubate at 28-30 °C for at least 1 h to recover.
Plate the cells on LB agar containing the appropriate antibiotic (i.e., 50 mg/L of kanamycin for pCAMBIA1302 for prokaryotic selection).
Incubate at 28-30 °C for 2-3 days.
Select one colony from the incubated culture.
Grow overnight in LB with appropriate selection (50 mg/L of kanamycin for pCAMBIA1302).
Cryopreserve the plasmid-containing strain using 50% glycerol at -80 °C.
Start C. vulgaris cultures 3 days before preparing A. tumefaciens cultures.
Spread 0.5 mL from a log phase culture (OD600 = 1.0) onto TAP agar plates (1.2% w/v agar).
Grow the spread culture for 5 days at 25 °C with illumination (50 µE/m²s).
Inoculate AGL-1 pCAMBIA1302 strain in a shaker flask by adding to 10 mL of LB media supplemented with 15 mM glucose, 20 mg/L rifampicin, and 50 mg/L kanamycin.
Incubate the inoculated culture at 28-30 °C and 250 rpm overnight.
Inoculate 1 mL of overnight A. tumefaciens culture into 50 mL of LB with 15 mM glucose, 20 mg/L rifampicin, and 50 mg/L kanamycin.
Incubate the new culture at 28-30 °C and 250 rpm until OD600 reaches 1.0.
Transfer the grown A. tumefaciens culture to a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the culture at 4000 x g for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant using a pipette.
Wash the cells twice with induction medium.
Resuspend the cells in induction medium to achieve an OD600 of 0.5.
Add 25 mL of induction media to the C. vulgaris plate containing approximately 5 x 10^6 cells.
Transfer the mixture to a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 4000 x g for 15 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Mix the algal cell pellet with 200 µL of bacterial suspension (OD600: 0.5).
Incubate the mixture in a rotary shaker at 21-25 °C and 150 rpm for 1 hour.
Spread 200 µL of the mixed culture onto induction media plates supplemented with 15 mM glucose.
Incubate the plates in the dark at 21-25 °C for 3 days.
Use 10 mL of TAP media supplemented with 400 mg/L cefotaxime or 20 mg/L tetracycline to collect microalgae after 3 days.
Incubate the collected culture in the dark at 21-25 °C for 2 days to eliminate A. tumefaciens from the culture.
Plate 500 µL of the culture onto selective media, e.g., TAP media supplemented with 20-70 mg/L of Hygromycin B (when using pCAMBIA1302) and 400 mg/L cefotaxime or 20 mg/L tetracycline.
Incubate at 21-25 °C in the dark for 2 days before placing them in an illuminated chamber.
Pick single colonies from the transformation plate.
Re-streak picked colonies on TAP agar plates supplemented with 400 mg/L cefotaxime or 20 mg/L tetracycline and 20-70 mg/L Hygromycin B.
Extract genomic DNA from a C. vulgaris transformant after subculturing at least twice from a single colony using a plant genomic DNA extraction kit.
Design primers for the mgfp5 region of the T-DNA (mgfp5-Fwd: 5' CCCATCTCATAAATAACGTC 3', and M13-Rev: 5' CAGGAAACAGCTATGAC 3').
Perform polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using a Q5 high-fidelity DNA polymerase master mix kit to validate transgene integration.
Use pCAMBIA1302 as a positive control.
Use wild-type C. vulgaris genomic DNA as a negative control.
To confirm that there is no pCAMBIA1302 present in the sample due to residual contamination by A. tumefaciens, use colony PCR.
Add a small amount of transformant cells to 10 µL of sterile water.
Boil at 98 °C for 15 min.
Use this as a template for PCR.
Design primers for a region outside of the T-DNA on pCAMBIA1302 (B1-Fwd: 5'AGTAAAGGAGAAGAACTTTTC 3' and B1-Rev: 5'CCTGATGCGGTATTTTCTC 3').
Use a boiled colony of A. tumefaciens AGL-1 (pCAMBIA1302) as a positive control.
Use a boiled colony of wild-type C. vulgaris as a negative control.
To confirm that there is no A. tumefaciens contamination present in the sample, use colony PCR.
Add a small amount of transformant cells to 10 µL of sterile water.
Boil at 98 °C for 15 min.
Use this as a template for PCR.
Design primers for the virE2 gene contained on the AGL-1 virulence plasmid (virE2-Fwd: 5' AGGGAGCCCTACCCG 3' and virE2-Rev: 5' GAACCAGCCTGGAGTTCG 3').
Use a boiled colony of A. tumefaciens AGL-1 (pCAMBIA1302) as a positive control.
Use a boiled colony of wild-type C. vulgaris as a negative control.
Inoculate each transformant from a log-phase maintenance culture or TAP agar slant into 50 mL of TAP supplemented with cefotaxime and Hygromycin B such that the starting OD600 = 0.1.
Incubate cultures at 25 °C at 150 rpm with photosynthetically active light.
Inoculate one culture with wild-type C. vulgaris and only 200 mg/L-1 cefotaxime as the negative control.
Take a sample every 24 hours to measure absorbance and fluorescence.
Use a black plate with a transparent bottom for simultaneous measurements.
Inoculate transformant (#50) from a log-phase maintenance culture into 300 mL of TAP supplemented with cefotaxime and Hygromycin B to reach OD680 = 0.1.
Incubate cultures at 25 °C at 150 rpm with photosynthetically active light.
Extract crude protein sample from the transformant (#50) and wild-type strains using lysis buffer.
Sonicate samples for 4 min.
Purify crude protein sample with a Ni-NTA resin through polypropylene columns.
Lyophilize the purified protein samples.
Resuspend lyophilized protein samples in lysis buffer for SDS-PAGE analysis.
